title: Release of Withheld Depreciation on CondoGuard Claims
content:
Claims manual section of the CondoGuard Unit-Owners Policy on depreciation withheld from an actual-cash-value payment.

## Recovery period

The holdback is released only when proof of completed repair or replacement is received no later than the depreciation recovery period that starts on the date of the initial actual-cash-value payment. The period is counted in calendar days from the date of the initial actual-cash-value payment, as the claim records show, and proof received on the last day is on time. Its length is the tier's depreciation recovery days.

## Amount released

The release is the smaller of the remaining holdback and the documented incurred cost, capped at the replacement-cost amount, less the actual cash value (the replacement-cost amount less the depreciation), and never below 0.00. Partial releases are allowed, and holdback left when the period ends is forfeited in one entry.

## Worksheet (hypothetical claim)

Replacement-cost amount 8000 USD, depreciation 1500 USD, so the actual cash value is 6500 USD and 1500 USD is withheld.

| Documented incurred cost (USD) | Incurred cost capped at the replacement-cost amount (USD) | Less the actual cash value (USD) | Remaining holdback (USD) | Release (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7400 | 7400 | 900 | 1500 | 900 |
| 9000 | 8000 | 1500 | 1500 | 1500 |
| 6000 | 6000 | below 0.00 | 1500 | 0.00 |

After the first row, 600 USD remains withheld; a further documented cost may release part or all of it within the period, and whatever is left when the period ends is forfeited.

## Boundary

With a recovery period of 180 days, proof received on the day that is 180 calendar days after the initial actual-cash-value payment is on time; proof received the day after is not.
